q: Two sponsors both need your time for urgent work on the same day. What is the best approach?
options: Make the conflict visible and let the priority be decided
Quietly work late and do both badly
why: Surfacing conflicts early lets the right people decide priorities and avoids surprises.

q: In the Eisenhower matrix, what should you do with work that is important but not urgent?
why: Important-not-urgent work should be scheduled so it isn't crowded out.

q: Why keep one master tracker across all your initiatives?
options: To see every deadline and next action in one place
why: One view of all work makes prioritization and context switching easier.

q: A project is behind schedule but a recovery plan is in place. What RAG status fits best?
why: Amber means at risk with a plan or a decision needed.

q: What is 'watermelon reporting'?
options: Reporting green on the outside while the project is really red
why: Watermelon reports hide real problems and destroy trust when the truth emerges.

q: Which status update is most useful to an executive?
options: UAT 82% complete; 3 high-severity defects open; decision needed on go-live date by Friday
We are working hard on many things
why: Specific numbers and a clear ask at the top are what decision makers need.

q: Where should the 'decision or help needed' appear in a status report?
options: Near the top, where readers will see it
Only in a separate email weeks later
why: Busy readers scan the top; put the ask there.

q: What does RAID stand for?
why: Some teams use Decisions for the D, but the most common form is Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies.

q: "The test environment is down today" should be logged as…
why: It has already happened and needs action now.

q: "The vendor might deliver the interface late" is…
why: It might happen in the future, so it is a risk.

q: What happens when a risk actually occurs?
options: It is deleted from the log
why: A realized risk is now an issue that needs action.

q: Which field is essential for every RAID entry?
why: Without an owner, nobody acts on it.

q: A risk has probability 4 and impact 5 on a 1–5 scale. What is its risk score?
why: Risk score = probability × impact = 4 × 5 = 20.

q: Starting vendor integration testing early to reduce the chance of late problems is an example of which response?
why: Mitigation reduces the probability or impact of a risk.

q: Buying insurance or signing a fixed-price contract is an example of which risk response?
why: Transferring moves the impact to a third party.

q: Removing a risky feature from scope so the risk can't occur is…
why: Avoidance changes the plan to eliminate the risk.

q: A risk is low impact and costly to address. What response is reasonable?
options: Accept it, possibly with a contingency plan
why: Acceptance is valid when the response costs more than the risk, but it should still be recorded.

q: What is a risk trigger?
options: A warning sign that the risk is about to occur
The person who caused the risk
why: Triggers signal when to activate the contingency plan.

q: Testing cannot start until the build is finished. What type of dependency is this?
why: B (testing) starts after A (build) finishes: finish-to-start.

q: Which escalation message is most effective?
options: Problem, impact, what we tried, options, recommendation, decision needed by Friday
This is a disaster, please help
Who is responsible for this mess?
why: Good escalations are short and bring options plus a recommendation.

q: When is escalation appropriate?
options: When the issue threatens objectives, you can't resolve it at your level, and you've tried directly
Before trying to solve it yourself
Never; BAs must solve everything alone
why: Escalation is for blockers beyond your authority, after a direct attempt.

q: How should you manage an external dependency on another team's API?
options: Agree a date and owner, and check in before the date
Wait until the date and then complain
why: Proactive check-ins catch slippage early.

q: What does a communication plan define for each audience?
options: What they need, format, frequency and owner
why: It ensures the right message reaches the right people in the right way at the right time.

q: How should communication differ for 'manage closely' versus 'monitor' stakeholders?
options: Frequent two-way contact versus occasional broadcasts
why: Communication intensity follows the stakeholder analysis.

q: What does ADKAR stand for?
why: ADKAR is Prosci's model of individual change.

q: Users have been trained but still don't use the new process because they don't see why it matters. Which ADKAR stage is the gap?
why: Training addresses Knowledge; it won't fix missing Awareness of the need or Desire to change.

q: What is the first step in Kotter's 8-step model?
why: Kotter starts by creating urgency, then builds a coalition and vision.

q: Respected users who help their peers adopt a new process are called…
why: Change champions (or change agents) support adoption within their teams.

q: Why does change management matter to a BA?
options: A solution only delivers value if people actually adopt it
why: Value comes from adoption, and BAs understand who is affected and how.
